title: Iran‐dom Acts
summary:
Iran‐dom Acts
With the tanker market largely tuned into the potential effects of a closure of the Straits of Hormuz, there is a chance that broadly sweeping policies to be enacted by the United States have been somewhat overshadowed. While sanctions with Iran are nothing new, the past few weeks have seen President Obama place increased emphasis on efforts to dissuade foreign central and private banks from dealing with the pariah state. Obama signed a new round of sanctions into law that have implications for participants in both petroleum and non‐petroleum transactions.

children.title: Pointing Fingers
children.summary: The majority of Iranian crude oil enters the market on a delivered basis via the National Iranian Tanker Company's (NITC) fleet of vessels: only about 20% of the 2.4 million barrels per day of net exports materialized through reported spot market transactions last year. The two charts below show the range of discharge locations for reported spot crude oil fixtures for 2002 and 2011.

children.title: UKC
children.summary: Based on an analysis of satellite data of NITC's fleet, a significant portion of Iranian exports is shipped to the Su‐Med pipeline in the Red Sea for end user markets in Europe. India has risen as a significant buyer as well.

children.title: Shoot First, Get Practical Later
children.summary: While Washington's stance on Tehran has been clear for quite some time, buy‐in from the international community is a lofty goal. So far the United States has even struggled to galvanize real support from allies simply due to their collective reluctance in severing a critical petroleum lifeline.
